summary: This paper develops a kinetic equation model for phonon down-conversion by normal-metal films, in which high-energy pair-breaking phonons scatter off electrons and lose energy below the qubit gap threshold. The authors solve the coupled equations for electron and phonon distributions in steady state, define a down-conversion efficiency $R_{m qp}$ comparing quasiparticle generation rates with and without the metal, and find that efficiency remains near-optimal ($>90\%$) over a finite metal thickness range with minimum thickness around $0.4\text{–}1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ for typical parameters.
motivation: Quasiparticle poisoning from high-energy impacts creates correlated error bursts threatening fault tolerance in superconducting qubit arrays; mitigating this requires understanding how normal metals can convert pair-breaking phonons to lower energies before they reach qubits.
method: The authors model a substrate–metal–superconductor stack using kinetic equations for phonon distributions in substrate and metal and electron distribution in metal, incorporating phonon transmission at interfaces ($\eta_{s m}, \eta_{m s}$) and electron-phonon collision integrals parameterized by coupling strengths $\tau_{\mathrm{el}}, \tau_{\mathrm{ph}}$. They solve the steady-state system analytically (deriving equilibrium-like forms) and numerically, using measured/calculated material parameters for Al, Nb, Ti, Cu, Au, Ag, Ta on Si and Al$_2$O$_3$.
result: For monochromatic injection at energy $\Omega_{\mathrm{inj}} > 2\Delta_{\mathrm{Al}} = 0.36\,\mathrm{meV}$, efficiency approaches $98.5\text{–}99\%$ at low injection rate when phonons escape the substrate faster than transmission into the metal ($\tau_{s m} \ll \tau_{\mathrm{es}} \approx 50\,\mu\mathrm{s}$), with Cu/Al/Si achieving highest resilience to increased injection rates; thin metal films fail to suppress the injected peak while thick films heat up, reducing efficiency below peak values near $d_m \sim 1\text{–}10\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ depending on parameters.
